Quirk-Friendly Design.text: Quirk-friendly design is the way cities are built for varied bodies and powers, and how far it reaches depends on how new a place is. Newer buildings have wide doors and high ceilings, train cars have reinforced seats and room for wings and tails, and public places offer oversized furniture. Everyday aids for people whose Quirks make ordinary life hard are common, many of them made by Detnerat, the big support-equipment maker: cooling sleeves, grip aids, tail and wing supports, filters and dampers. Older buildings and rural towns lag behind, with narrow stairs, low doorways and fixed seats, and heteromorph customers notice. Shops that stock clothes and seating for every body type advertise the fact, and accessible design is a selling point for new apartments.
